title: Copperline Systems — Renewal, Governance & Edge Provisioning Check-in
summary: 30-minute renewal check-in focused on confirming Copperline's capacity uplift timing, discussing VPC/KMS governance items for the private deployment pilot, and clarifying billing amendment options. Agreement to run a short throughput test on staged geocluster and to share an updated pricing amendment. Some audio dropouts during the second quarter of the call; a few words transcribed imprecisely.
topics: Private deployment (VPC) onboarding, KMS integration and audit logs
Regional onramp: EU-West staging then APAC pilot
Proof-of-work: 1-hour throughput/latency test and failover run

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-08
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~38 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Priya (Copperline CTO), Ethan (Head of Platform), Jordan (SRE), Avery (Procurement)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out the time, appreciate it. We'll keep this tight — objective is to confirm the renewal amendment timing, the capacity uplift spec, and run through the VPC/KMS governance asks you raised. Daniel and I will follow up with the tech playbook and pricing. Does that sound good Priya?

[00:16] Priya: Yeah that sounds good, Maya. Quick context — we're roughly at 70% of current baseline during peak for search and question-answer workloads, so the plan we discussed internally is to move to 2.5x baseline for Q1 and then top up later in the year. Procurement wants to see costs and the contract change.

[00:40] Ethan: And just to add, latency matters for EU customers — sub-120ms P50 is our soft target. We'll need the EU staging to be representative before we flip traffic.

[01:05] Daniel: Got it. For the 2.5x baseline, we usually recommend a dedicated pool with automated burst policies. We can show a few options: steady-reserved capacity versus stepped ramp with monthly top-ups. The performance profile in EU should hold; we do kernel selection and regional routing. There was a note about VPC — can you expand on the KMS/HSM constraint?

[01:35] Priya: Sure. Our security team prefers HSM-backed keys for any patient-identifiable data. We'll want audit logs shipped to our SIEM, and SSO/SAML mappings for admin roles. Also need retention policies spelled out for logs.

[02:02] Maya: That's fine — Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and audit exports. HSM via partnered KMS providers is supported for the Private plane; we'll double-check the exact vendor compatibility. We'll add the audit-log retention options into the security appendix in the amendment.

[02:25] Avery: Quick procurement note — if there's a clear amendment showing cost delta and a fixed commitment period, we can route without another RFP. But legal needs the SLAs in writing, and finance needs monthly burn estimates.

[02:47] Maya: Understood. We'll include a pricing sheet with monthly burn projections for both options. Daniel, can you speak to the failover policy if a geocluster hits capacity?

[03:05] Daniel: Yes — our standard is smart routing with automatic fallback to a compatible model variant or another region based on the policy. For private deployments we can set hard failover windows or soft degrade with partial request shedding. For your use case, I'd recommend a soft degrade threshold at 85% followed by reroute to the next nearest geocluster. We can tune that.

[03:38] Jordan: So that reroute — does that preserve prompt state? We rely on KV cache continuity for multi-turn sessions.

[03:52] Daniel: Good catch. For sessions where KV cache matters, we support persistent KV state replication for nearby geoclusters in the same geo-failover ring. There's a cost delta there — extra storage and replication overhead. We'll add a small estimate in the pricing doc.

[04:15] Priya: Okay that helps. Also on metrics — we need token-level cost breakdown and traceability to route decisions. Can that be exported?

[04:28] Maya: Yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost breakdowns per route/model, and you can export CSVs or push metrics to your telemetry via webhook. We'll include the export config in the playbook.

[04:45] Ethan: One of our blockers is KMS integration for the private control plane. We use AWS KMS with multi-account setup; ideally we hand you an ARN and a cross-account role and you're done. Does Redwood support cross-account KMS and BYOK?

[05:03] Daniel: We do. BYOK and cross-account ARNs are supported in Private. We'll need the KMS ARN and an IAM role with the encryption permissions. We'll also request an allowlist of IPs for the VPC peering. Jordan, maybe you can share the specifics after this call?

[05:21] Jordan: Yep will do. I'll pull the ARN and the VPC CIDRs.

[05:30] Maya: Great. Next up — region ramp. You mentioned EU-West staging then APAC pilot?

[05:38] Priya: Correct. We want EU first for regulation/residency and then APAC as a lower throughput pilot in March. Ideally EU staging runs by Jan 25 so we can validate before end of month.

[05:52] Maya: Jan 25 is tight but doable. We'll propose a 1-hour throughput and failover run during the week of Jan 18 — Redwood SE + your SREs run it together. Daniel, can you outline what we'll need to execute the run?

[06:05] Daniel: We'll need a shared test harness (we'll provide the script), a sample prompt set (you provide production-ish prompts), and network connectivity to the staging geocluster. Also, KV cache warm-up instructions — so the run is representative. I'll upload the harness and sample commands to the shared folder.

[06:28] Ethan: What's the expected timeline to interpret the results? We want to make decisions quickly.

[06:34] Daniel: We can usually deliver an initial read within 24 hours of the test: latency percentiles, token throughput, and observed cost per 1k tokens with current quantization profile. If any regressions show up, we can iterate the kernel/profile settings.

[06:50] Avery: From procurement — can you flag any contract terms that change materially with the 2.5x uplift? Things like termination clauses or minimum commitment durations.

[07:01] Maya: We'll surface the differences clearly. In short, higher reserved capacity gives you a lower unit price and an SLA backstop for capacity. The amendment will show both options: a 12-month commit at 2.5x with a lower effective token price, or a 6-month stepped ramp with slightly higher unit rates. We'll also include rollback windows.

[07:22] Priya: Sounds good. On the security appendix — HSM compatibility is crucial. Maya, can you confirm supported HSM/KMS vendors?

[07:33] Maya: We support major providers — AWS KMS (HSM-backed), Google Cloud KMS, and partner HSM vendors via our private partner integration. I'll confirm the exact vendor list and any limitations in the appendix.

[07:47] Daniel: Also to call out — audit logs can be exported to your SIEM in near-real time, but retention beyond 90 days is usually an add-on. We'll price that out.

[08:00] Jordan: For KV replication — earlier you said there was a cost delta. Can you ballpark?

[08:06] Daniel: Very rough — think additional 8-12% on top of the storage/replication for KV state for replicated rings. We'll model it in the pricing doc per GB replicated.

[08:20] Priya: Ok that's fine, as long as it's spelled out.

[08:28] Maya: Quick question — are you considering multi-tenant hosted vs Private for part of the fleet?

[08:36] Priya: We want most sensitive data on Private; some stateless features could run on Hosted to save cost, but legal wants a clear boundary.

[08:49] Maya: That's a common hybrid pattern. We'll show a recommended split in the technical appendix and cost model: Private for identifiable data flows, hosted for anonymized workloads.

[09:02] (small audio dropout)

[09:18] Ethan: One more technical — can the dedicated pool autoscale faster for bursts? Our traffic is spiky around marketing pushes.

[09:26] Daniel: Autoscale can be tuned with burst windows and pre-warmed nodes. There's a trade-off: faster autoscale reduces latency but increases baseline cost to maintain warm capacity. We can configure a burst buffer that triggers at sustained CPU/token thresholds.

[09:47] Priya: Do you have any examples from similar customers?

[09:51] Maya: We ran a similar pattern with a retail customer — they used a 20% pre-warm buffer and saved on cold-start latency; cost increased by about 6% but reduced user-facing errors. We'll anonymize and include that case study in the follow-up.

[10:08] Jordan: For the staging run, will we be able to simulate cross-region failover?

[10:14] Daniel: Yes — we'll orchestrate a failover step in the script so you can see how KV replication and routing behave. We'll also capture traces for the end-to-end flow.

[10:27] Priya: Good. Procurement question — if we sign for 12 months at 2.5x, is there a mid-term renegotiation clause?

[10:36] Maya: We usually include an amendment path with a mutual-review at 6 months. If substantial uplift is needed, we can do a rebaseline with 60 days' notice. We'll put that in the legal section.

[10:49] Avery: That's acceptable. Also need a contact for incident escalation during onboarding.

[10:54] Daniel: I'll be the technical contact for the onboarding window and we'll add a dedicated support channel for your SREs.

[11:02] Maya: Great — next steps recap: Redwood sends pricing amendment + playbook by Jan 12; SE uploads test harness and we'll schedule the staging run week of Jan 18; Copperline provides KMS ARNs, VPC CIDRs, and procurement window by Jan 14. Anything else?

[11:19] Priya: One small ask — can you include a short runbook for rolling back traffic if the failover introduces regressions? We want explicit steps.

[11:26] Daniel: Absolutely. We'll include rollback steps and example CLI/API calls.

[11:33] Priya: Perfect. Thanks everyone.

[11:37] Maya: Thanks — we'll follow up with the docs. We'll set a calendar hold for the staging run; Daniel will reach out to coordinate time zones.

[11:45] (meeting ends)

Notes: occasional transcription glitches: "KV" sometimes appears as "K-V"; a short dropout at ~09:02 caused missing 10s. References to internal decks and playbook: "staging-playbook-v2.pdf" (link to be shared) and shared folder "Copperline_Redwood_01".
footer_notes: Referenced artifacts: staging-playbook-v2.pdf, Copperline_Redwood_01 (shared drive). Pricing options: 12mo commit @ 2.5x baseline vs 6mo stepped ramp. Follow-up: Redwood to share amendment + test harness.
